LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 5.3.1. WORD CLASSES: COMPARATIVE AND SUPERLATIVE ADJECTIVES

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.3: Grammar in Use 5.3.1. Word Classes: Comparative and Superlative Adjectives
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 5.3.1. Word Classes: Comparative and Superlative Adjectives, part of Strand 5 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How do we compare different people, places, and things? 2. Why are comparisons important in life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in Use 5.3.1. Word Classes: Comparative and Superlative Adjectives together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to Learn: Learner develops the skill of organising own learning as he/she searches online or offline for examples of

comparative and superlative adjectives.

● Self-efficacy: Learners develop planning skills as they use flashcards to categorise adjectives into comparatives and superlatives

successfully.

Values:
● Love: is nurtured as the learner portrays a caring attitude while using adjectives in the comparative and superlative forms to express

family relations.

Link to other Subjects

The learner is able to relate the concept of comparative and superlative adjectives to their day to day communication.
